additional_info.subject: RE: ID0453904-DC/Si-D/NL-[MP / R6 170002078] Charger communication issue CRM:03056000104
additional_info.body:
Dear Daan,
Glad to hear that everything works fine now!
So, I took a look at the charger, let me answer your questions:
The charger has an installed power capacity of 300kW
Each outlet is limited from SCB to 270kW
If ELMS is configured and active, the power setpoints coming from the ELMS will always overrule the outlet power limitation from SCB. If the power limitation from SCB on DC is 270kW, but the ELMS is (for example) setting 140kW as power setpoint on DC2, the charger will follow ELMS setpoint.
I checked some logs and for example yesterday the "PlimELMSOutlet" was set at 4kW, hence the EVSEMaxPower is following ELMS limitation:
If you want to change the power setpoint from ELMS, this has to be done from your side, unfortunately I cannot support with that.
If you want to change the power limit of the outlets themselves from SCB, this can be done form anyone who has 3rd level access on SCB, by changing the PLC configuration. In case you do not have access, you can open a service ticket.
I hope I provided clarification to your doubts. Please let me know if you have further questions, otherwise I will proceed to close this ticket.
With kind regards,

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0453904-DC/Si-D/NL-[MP / R6 170002078] Charger communication issue CRM:03056000104
additional_info.body:
Dear Daan,
As per stated in the ELMS manual for Sicharge D and in the table 3.2 you reported, if the
A_ELMS_LL
(Active Load limitation) is set to 0, the setpoint G_ActPwrLimit_SP is enforced as a new active power input limit for the whole charger, and the charger and the outlets will not consider ELMS limits even if setpoints were transmitted on the corresponding fallback- & setpoint registers.
This means that, in case of charging on a single outlet, the charger is limiting the outlet power to 270kW (as per outlet power limitation from SCB, not on the installed power of 300kW), and it will follow the EVs current request. If the charger is performing a parallel charging, the outlet power limitation will be set by the charger itself, according to converter distribution for High Flex configuration of the charger, and internal logic "First-in-First-Served".
In conclusion, I confirm to you that now the Active Load limitation from ELMS is off since 13.10:
2025-10-13T07:57:15.381109+00:00 [FW060103G1] swcpu [user:debug] [4127] [ELM]  ELMS -> SICHARGE (control): Load limitation active = false
The charger is therefore not limited by the ELMS and allocating power according to internal logic.
I hope I provided clarification to your doubts. If there are no further doubts on the ELMS power limitation, I would then proceed to close the ticket.
With kind regards,
